justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: Time-series traces are plotted continuously along a Days axis (0–5) with regular spacing; no abrupt jumps or skipped tick values are visible.
Amplitude axis shows smoothly varying traces with no signs of discontinuity, irregular tick spacing, or omitted ranges; no break mark is present or needed.
Heatmap x-axis is an indexed set of circadian parameters (1–7) with regular labeling and no skipped or non-sequential values; no axis break is apparent or required.
Heatmap y-axis similarly shows regular, sequential parameter indices; the color scale is continuous and there is no evidence of omitted ranges or required break markers.
Cartoon growth curves use Days on the x-axis with evenly spaced tick marks (e.g., 1–4); there is no sudden skip or compressed region indicating an unlabeled break.
Cell number axis is drawn continuously with smoothly varying curves; no discontinuity or non-linear jump is indicated that would require a break marker.
Dose–response cartoon shows a continuous dose axis (Dose, μM) without visible skipped numeric ticks or abrupt spacing changes that would indicate an omitted range.
Response (growth inhibition) is plotted continuously; there are no sudden vertical jumps or compressed regions in the axis scale requiring a break marker.
Gene expression and mutation heatmaps use indexed axes (cell lines / clock genes) with regular grid spacing; no skipped indices or axis discontinuities are visible.
Heatmap rows/columns are evenly spaced; color mapping provides continuous range and there is no indication of an omitted axis region that would need a break marker.
PCA scatter plots show PC1 along the x-axis with regular tick spacing and continuous placement of points; no skipped numeric ranges or compressions require a break mark.
PC2 (and PC axes in the 3D inset) are displayed with even tick spacing and continuous data distribution; there is no visual discontinuity or non-sequential tick labeling.
The 3D schematic shows a third parameter axis (Parameter #1/#2/#3) with continuous point placement and no evidence of omitted ranges or axis breaks.
